The v1.2 workflows describe conditional inference under an explicitly selected
probability law. They do not turn a historical likelihood score into a normalized
sampling model, or an external tree sample into a joint Bayesian analysis.

## Fit and inspect one contract

The following uses the bundled 19-tip Hawaiian *Psychotria* example. The code is
shown without automatically running a costly analysis during documentation builds.

```{r fit, eval=FALSE}
library(RustBEARS)
run <- define_BioGeoBEARS_run(
  trfn=system.file('extdata/Psychotria_5.2_ultrametric.newick', package='RustBEARS'),
  geogfn=system.file('extdata/Psychotria_geog.data', package='RustBEARS'),
  max_range_size=4, calc_ancprobs=TRUE, print_optim=FALSE)
run$likelihood_conditioning <- 'tip_survival'
run$root_prior <- define_root_prior('uniform_nonnull')
run$num_cores_to_use <- 1L
run <- readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(run)
dec <- bears_optim_run(run)
runj <- run
runj$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table['j','type'] <- 'free'
runj$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table['j',c('init','est')] <- .01
decj <- bears_optim_run(runj)
```

`tip_survival` is Contract A. Contract B, `unconditional_complete`, permits empty
tips and needs `allow_null_tips=TRUE`. Contract C, `legacy_unconditioned`, retains
the old score and root-weight scale. R defaults to StrictF64; request LegacyF32
explicitly for historical comparisons. Prepared samplers reject changed input files.

## Profiles, bootstrap and model averaging

```{r inference, eval=FALSE}
intervals <- profile_ci(dec, params='e', include_onesided_zero_ref=TRUE)
test <- bootstrap_lrt(dec, decj, n_boot=399L,
                      checkpoint_file='psychotria-bootstrap.rds', seedval=42L)
test$pval_failure_bounds
test$pval_mc_ci95
average <- model_average(list(dec, decj), num_maps=500L, seedval=42L)
```

Profiles reoptimize nuisance parameters, expose zero/box boundary statuses and
refuse numerically uncertified endpoints. Contract C returns support intervals.
Bootstrap failures remain in the planned denominator. Failure bounds and Monte
Carlo intervals answer different questions. A fixed-null-threshold power
surrogate is separate from fully nested test power. Akaike weights use fitted
parameters; they are not Bayesian model probabilities. AICc uses tip count as
its stated sample-size convention and may be undefined for very small trees.

## External trees and mapping precision

```{r trees, eval=FALSE}
multiple <- fit_over_trees(run, 'external-posterior.trees',
  models=c('DEC','DEC+J'), likelihood_conditioning='tip_survival',
  checkpoint_file='tree-fits.rds', bsm_maps_per_tree=500L)
maps <- runBSM(dec, NULL, bsm_engine='native_whole_tree', seedval=42L,
  target_rmcse=.05, min_maps=200L, batch_size=200L, max_maps=5000L)
precision <- bsm_diagnostics(maps, tree_target='fixed_sample')
```

Every tree needs the complete model set. Failed trees are isolated, with
complete-case means and deterministic probability missing-fit bounds. Event
counts are unbounded and cannot use those same bounds. Exact-clade and MRCA
summaries differ; MRCA results include excess-tip counts. Root incoming-branch
probabilities remain undefined.

Mapping precision defaults to the fixed supplied tree sample. A population
target requires explicit independent or ordered-MCMC provenance. Route decisions
use paired differences: near ties require the whole interval inside the practical
equivalence band; resolved differences require it wholly outside on one side.
The intervals are exploratory per-comparison intervals without simultaneous,
rank-selection or optional-stopping coverage guarantees. Rare events are marked
not assessed. Stop reasons are reported independently.

The initial uncertainty scope is single-layer standard DEC, DIVALIKE and
BAYAREALIKE families with/without J and validated x/w modifiers. Fossil hooks,
time stratification and trait coupling remain explicitly disabled in these new
workflows. Full reproducible R and Python examples, in Chinese and English,
are provided in the repository's `docs` directory.
